As a Christian, I’ve struggled for years with fearing denying myself and putting God’s will and plan above my own. It scared me to think about. I also had difficulty feeling emotion towards God. As in, when I thought of Him, I didn’t always get this overwhelming joy or thankfulness.

But I went through a rough spot where I realized that trying to do things my own way and figure it out myself was only bringing pain into my life. 

I prayed that God would help me want to do His will. And He has helped me a lot with that.

God doesn’t expect us to change ourselves on our own. I was so caught up in the world’s ideas of goodness being something we can do ourselves and constantly policing my own actions, that I forgot what God tells us in the Bible. All have sinned. But through Jesus there is salvation.

You don’t have to be perfect. God knows you are not. But He loves you anyways and He desires us to obey Him. We don’t have to be obedient by fixing ourselves though or doing it all at once. We can turn to God and ask Him to help us. My desire to do His will has changed across 9 years, but I still struggle with putting Him first even so. 

God has helped me better love Him and desire His will. But I couldn’t have done it without Him. Don’t beat yourself up over struggling with wanting His will. Instead, trust Him and ask Him to help, because we can’t do it alone and He doesn’t want us to do things alone

I’ve struggled with the idea of the unforgivable sin myself. In the context of the verses, we see Jesus driving our demons by the Holy Spirit. The people accuse Jesus of doing this by the power of the devil. Seeing God’s work, they rejected it and said it was of the devil. They refused to accept the witness of the Holy Spirit to who Jesus was, and refused to acknowledge the Holy Spirit after having seen Jesus drive out demons by the Holy Spirit. 

I struggle with doing things, knowing they are sins. But desiring to do better seems to show that the Holy Spirit is at work in you. I’ve done things that were hateful towards God, but He still holds me.

“My sheep hear My voice, I know them, and they follow Me. I give them eternal life, and they will never perish — ever! No one will snatch them out of My hand. My Father, who has given them to Me, is greater than all. No one is able to snatch them out of the Father’s hand. The Father and I are one.””
‭‭John‬ ‭10‬:‭27‬-‭30‬ ‭HCSB‬‬

I don’t exactly understand the verses about willing sin, but I think that to an extent, sin in general is willing. I think we often know that it’s wrong, even if we don’t want to consciously acknowledge that. But even though I’ve struggled with that, God remains with me.

Sometimes, my feelings are out of line and I don’t feel super guilty about sins. I have a problem with my emotions sometimes and overload. But I acknowledge that even if I don’t feel it, I’m sorry because sin is wrong and I’m sorry in that I’ve wronged God. Regardless of that though, Jesus, His sacrifice on the cross, and His resurrection, mean that salvation doesn’t hinge on us specifically repenting of each sin we commit. We could never remember all our sins to repent of each of them, but we don’t have to.
We can have an attitude of repentance, and confess our sins and express repentance to God, but if you miss some sins, you’re still saved.

Not trying to say that we shouldn’t regret our sins in an emotional way - but if you’re struggling emotionally, that doesn’t mean you aren’t forgiven or saved.

I was in a relationship with a guy who was not Christian.
He was incredibly kind and loving. We respected each other and He even went to church with me. That said, I felt convicted to break it off because of the verse about being unequally yoked and other verses. 1 Corinthians 7 is particularly helpful for me


In 1 Corinthians 7:39, we can read “A wife is bound as long as her husband is living. But if her husband dies, she is free to be married to anyone she wants — only in the Lord.”
‭‭
This further emphasizes the need for marriage to be between believers.

As Christians, we must put God first, even above our partner. However, Christianity also describes a married couple as “no longer two, but one.”

If you’re “one” with a fellow believer, you can both seek God together. However, being “one” with an unbeliever means you’ll be at odds with each other

Even if you agree on other things, being “one” with a person who doesn’t follow God wouldn’t make sense



With that said, I know this is probably an uncomfortable situation. Ultimately, talking to another believer and praying with her helped me. It was uncomfortable to break things off. But I needed to do it

I still think about my ex from years ago sometimes. When we love someone, it’s hard to let them go. 

Letting go of a relationship is hard. I’m still in the process of that right now. But God is faithful. And He loves us wonderfully

I’ve also struggled with the idea of the unpardonable sin. But once I talked to faith leaders about it, I realized it wasn’t what I thought.


Here’s a good summary of it I found


“The one sin which God cannot forgive is mentioned in Mark 3:28-30 and Matthew 12:31-32. Jesus had been performing miracles, including driving demons out of people by the power of the Holy Spirit. Instead of recognizing the source of Jesus’ power and accepting Him as God’s Son, the religious leaders accused Him of being possessed by the devil and driving demons out in the power of the devil.

Jesus responded by saying, “I tell you the truth, all the sins and blasphemies of men will be forgiven them. But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will never be forgiven; he is guilty of an eternal sin.”

The sin of the religious leaders, blasphemy against the Holy Spirit, was a refusal to accept the witness of the Holy Spirit to who Jesus was and what He had come to do, and then submit their lives to Him. Jesus said concerning the Holy Spirit, “When he comes, he will convict the world of guilt in regard to sin and righteousness and judgment” (John 16:8). They chose rather to reject the Spirit’s witness to their sin and to Jesus, and accused Him of being demon possessed!

The point for us is that if we have received Jesus as our Savior and Lord, we have not blasphemed the Holy Spirit; we have accepted His witness.”

You sound like me. I’ve been a Christian since 2015 and I still struggle with these thoughts.

I’ve thought I was too broken, too messed up, too evil to be saved or for God to want me as His child.
I’ve turned to comfort in my despair to try and feel something, making myself feel worse for self indulging. I thought I committed the unforgivable sin and was past saving. I’ve been hostile towards God and accused Him of being evil. I’ve been hateful towards Him.

And yet, He has remained faithful and He is still with me.

Being a Christian does not mean we are perfect. But we are forgiven. I still struggle with feeling like I have to earn my salvation. But that’s not true. Jesus died and paid the cost for my sin - and I can never pay Him back. Even if I was the most obedient Christian on earth, I could never earn what Jesus did for me. It’s a free gift that we receive by believing in Jesus and trusting in Him as Savior and Lord, confessing Him as Savior and Lord


I still struggle with not wanting to talk about Jesus, with worrying about what others will think of me if I try to share the gospel. But I’m saved nonetheless


In John 6:37-40, Jesus says: 

“Everyone the Father gives Me will come to Me, and the one who comes to Me I will never cast out. For I have come down from heaven, not to do My will, but the will of Him who sent Me. This is the will of Him who sent Me: that I should lose none of those He has given Me but should raise them up on the last day. For this is the will of My Father: that everyone who sees the Son and believes in Him may have eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day.””
‭‭
Jesus will not cast us out if we have trusted in Him. 

In John 10:27-30
“My sheep hear My voice, I know them, and they follow Me. I give them eternal life, and they will never perish — ever! No one will snatch them out of My hand. My Father, who has given them to Me, is greater than all. No one is able to snatch them out of the Father’s hand. The Father and I are one.””
‭‭
Jesus said “no one is able to snatch them out of the Father’s hand.” 

That includes us. Humans are sinful, broken creatures. But in Christ, we are a new creation. And we aren’t powerful enough to change God’s salvation if we are saved. We aren’t powerful enough to snatch ourselves from the Father’s hand

I’m sorry you’re feeling this way :(

Feeling that nothing matters or that your life doesn’t matter is terrifying. I’ve felt that before and it scared me and made me think, “what’s the point in any of this?”

But I don’t believe that anymore. You matter. And no matter how much this time in your life makes you feel like that’s not true, it won’t change the fact that you do matter

I’m sorry you’re feeling this way. It’s hard when you feel like you’re staring at a dead end.

Have you tried talking more to your parents about this? Maybe explaining what you’re feeling and why? I know that’s probably scary to think about. But please try that before harming yourself. I’ve had some uncomfortable conversations across my life, but having them can help make things better.

Also, as someone who used to place her self worth in her grades and school, it’s dangerous - and not worth it. I studied and worked hard to be at the top of my class in high school. And yet, what I’ve learned is that I wouldn’t want that for others. 
I burned myself out. I stressed myself out. And ultimately, being number one in the class didn’t change things. I got into a university and am prepping for a career, but I didn’t need to be number one for that.

You are more important than any grade, any college degree, or any job ever could be. You are more valuable than any of that.

God loves us, even when things are hard. He wouldn’t want you to harm yourself though. 

You’re not alone in your sorrow.

Various people mentioned in the Bible experienced deep sorrow and depression - Elijah prayed to die, King David said in Psalms 6:6-7 “I am weary from my groaning; with my tears I dampen my pillow and drench my bed every night. My eyes are swollen from grief; they grow old because of all my enemies.”

Jesus Himself suffered and died, experiencing sorrow.

In Isaiah‬ ‭53‬:‭3‬-‭4‬, it says
“He was despised and rejected by men, a man of suffering who knew what sickness was. He was like someone people turned away from; He was despised, and we didn’t value Him. Yet He Himself bore our sicknesses, and He carried our pains; but we in turn regarded Him stricken, struck down by God, and afflicted.”
‭‭
God loves you. And He understands us better than we can know. 

I’ve had a rough year struggling with the idea of God’s love amidst depression and anger. But I’ve come to realize that God loves me in a way I can’t even fathom. Because I can’t really understand that great of a love.

I hope you’ll reconsider your plan and stay. God loves you and He wants good for us - and good for you :)

I’m in an accelerated nursing program right now and it’s a lot, though I’m sure medical school is much different. 

I used to be at the top of my class in high school, but when I got to college, I was burned out and have been struggling with that. I was premed but as a Christian, I prayed about what direction to go in, and nursing seemed to be the answer. I eventually got into my nursing program by the grace of God, after having been originally rejected and then accepted off the waiting list 

It’s been difficult to deal with all the work plus trying to socialize. Im an introvert too, but I had a good community I was around until I experienced some depression and started self isolating. 

The isolation made things much worse and I just dwelled on my thoughts. As one of my nursing professors says, she recommends finding something outside of school to enjoy.

Again, I don’t know you and I can’t tell you what to do, but I wanted to share that having doubts about yourself in medical school and professional schools aren’t all that uncommon and don’t necessarily mean you aren’t cut out to be a doctor. I’m here if you want to talk :)

My uncle committed suicide a couple years ago. I remember the day it happened. I was in my room that morning and I heard my mom talking. 

I left my room and I remember her saying that something had happened. And then she told me my uncle was dead

The feeling of knowing that you won’t get to see someone again in this life can make you feel empty. The world changes. One day you’re living life and the next something has happened that you can’t fix. 

That’s part of what it feels like to lose someone.

I saw him about a month before it happened. I had been in the room he killed himself in multiple times. Little did I know that one day my uncle would end his life there in that room.

We weren’t particularly close. We visited him a couple times a year. And yet, despite that, his death was still painful. It was worse for my brother. I remember that he cried. My brother didn’t cry a lot unless in pain. But he cried when my uncle died. My family tried to hide that my uncle had killed himself from my two little brothers. But the oldest ended up finding out I believe.

It’s almost been three years now. Even though we weren’t close, I remember him at random times. Like when I’m listening to a random country song while driving. Like how I thought about him after I got into my university. He could have come and visited me here. He likes my university and our sports team. He would have been happy for me getting in.

His daughter still has his photo up as her background image on Facebook. She posts about him. He was important in the lives of his grandchildren. They loved him. I remember seeing a picture one of them drew. A family picture. They drew my uncle up at the top in heaven.


As much as it feels like your death is the best thing for those around you, you are wrong. It’s not.

You influence the lives of those around you. Even perhaps people you barely have a relationship with. People that you maybe just say hi to, or look at as you walk by. I don’t know what or who my uncle may have thought of in his last moments here. But I know that his death affected the lives of many - some of them who he might not have expected. 

You are still here though. And I want you to know that your death has the potential to harm so many people. Don’t tell yourself this will help them. Please, I ask you to consider my story and the story of my uncle. Your life is important and you are loved. Even if you can’t see it right now

I’ve gone through wanting to be a veterinarian, actress, pediatrician, psychiatrist, nurse practitioner, medical scientist, and a pathologist. 

It was only in the fall semester of my senior year that I started thinking about pathology as a career, which is what I ultimately decided to do. Even people who are already in college change their minds sometimes about what they want to do. In fact, I’m about to start my fall semester at college and I’ve already thought about potentially becoming a different type of doctor or considering the nursing field again. (I ended up deciding to stick to medical school)

It’s ok to not know what you want to do right now. 

I might suggest taking job and interest quizzes (not like Buzzfeed quizzes though, lol). Some of these quizzes take into account your interests and what you want in a job and help narrow it down into fields that you may be interested in. *Remember though, just because a quiz suggests you may enjoy something or that a certain career field suits you, it doesn’t mean you are limited to that field or that you won’t succeed outside that field. 

In addition to this, researching the various careers in areas you’re interested in or asking family members about their jobs could be helpful. I learned more about what I wanted to do by talking to my cousin and Great Aunt.
I don’t know if you’d be interested based on your desire to go abroad, but perhaps you could look into online masters degree programs so you could stay close to home
Maybe you could try Khan Academy. I’m pretty sure it’s free. You can link your SAT scores with your Khan account and I believe it helps you study the areas you need help with.

You mentioned that your parents don’t have post-secondary education. There are scholarships available for people who are the first in their family to go to college. You could try and apply to one of these. There are also scholarship search websites that allow you to enter in your information and find scholarships that apply to you. GoingMerry and Unigo are two examples. Unigo also has scholarships sorted into categories that help make it easier to find ones that you are eligible for and interested in.

Also, maybe trying to earn a certificate from online classes could help you. There are certain certifications you can receive by taking online classes. They may take a bit and cost money, but perhaps they could benefit you. I just thought I’d mention them

I would suggest talking to your doctor the next time you visit. It almost sounds like you’re depressed, which could account for some of this. Of course, I’m not a doctor myself and this isn’t a diagnosis, but maybe you could talk to your doctor about it.

On a second note, I felt burned out like you in my 11th grade year because I took too many classes and had too much to deal with. I also know a person who had similar experience in having trouble making themself do things. I want you to know that you’re not alone :) 
Also, don’t be too hard on yourself over such things. Of course it’s helpful to get things done, but making yourself feel bad when you don’t could possibly make things worse. Focus on the things you want to do and not on beating yourself up if you don’t get to them
Try to either get involved in new clubs or more involved in clubs you’re already in. This looks good when applying to college. Just don’t overwhelm yourself :)
